newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - TAB powerless to stop betting breaches.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - TAB powerless to stop betting breaches.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 29 - The TAB admitted on Tuesday it was virtually powerless to prevent sportspeople betting on matches they were involved in, NZPA reports.
TAB manager of corporate affairs Jim Leach said it viewed alleged breaches of sports betting irregularities by players or team officials seriously because of the principle involved.
However, policing the regulations was very, very difficult.
"In reality it's very, very difficult," Leach told NZPA.

"I wouldn't say it was totally impossible, but if someone seriously set out to place a bet on a match they were involved in, clearly they could do it. You have to look at the realities -- they can get someone else to place the bet for them, for example."

The Marlborough Rugby Football Union is meeting tonight to discuss allegations that a player wagered $100 at 6-1 odds for Marlborough to beat Mid-Canterbury by 12 or fewer points in their NPC third division semifinal on October 19. Marlborough won the match 34-22.
New Zealand Rugby Football Union (NZRFU) chairman Richie Guy yesterday said an investigation had been launched into an alleged breach of its sports betting regulations involving a Marlborough player.

Guy later revealed that another third division team Wanganui was to be investigated after he received a telephone call alleging a possible breach by players involved in their third division final against Marlborough in Blenheim last Saturday.
Leach said it was largely up to the NZRFU to police its sports betting regulations.
"It comes down to the rugby union policing it. We monitor the betting patterns and if there is any serious betting going on we look at that carefully. We monitor every significant bet."

Leach said players and officials were not breaking any laws by gambling on matches they were involved in, but it was contrary to the principle of the agreement reached by the NZRFU and the TAB when they drew up a sports betting contract in July.
"It is a matter of principle, but I think the whole matter has been blown out of proportion."
Marlborough captain Rob Penney would welcome any NZRFU investigation.
He is confident his team have not breached the union's betting regulations.
Penney, who is also the Marlborough union's executive officer, said the accusations against his team were groundless.
"I can guarantee it's just a pub story that's got on a bit of a roll.
"Obviously, legally we're not allowed to bet on our own games, and it would be hugely inappropriate if someone did so.
"I hope someone does come across from the NZRFU and talk to us about it because these stories have to be nipped in the bud.
"We know the legal ramifications. Guys betting in that scenario would be extremely foolish."

NZRFU regulations allow for a broad range of penalties, including the imposition of a fine or suspension, on individuals or teams found to have gambled on the outcome of matches they were involved in.
"We have to determine what happened," Guy said.
"What is alleged clearly infringes our gambling regulations."
Penney said he was aware of a Marlborough supporter who had been placing bets on the outcome of the province's matches.
"But it had absolutely nothing to do with the team."
